html:
The Tonkawa Tribe of Oklahoma lives on a small reservation near the town of Tonkawa in Kay County, northern Oklahoma. The Tonkawa were originally bison hunters and gatherers of central Texas, and some were gathered into Spanish missions there with peoples such as the Sana.

In the 1800s they often sided with Texas and the US against the Comanche, their old enemies. In 1859 they were moved north to Indian Territory, and in 1862 a force of Indians allied to the Union attacked them at their agency and killed a large share of the tribe. The survivors went back to Texas. In 1884 and 1885 they were moved again, for good, to the Oakland Agency in what became Oklahoma, where the tribe survived as a small community.
